subject: research/ambient-goldaudit
professional: a reviewer at a statistics / ML venue (e.g. UAI, AISTATS, or JASA for measurement error) who works on latent-class / Dawid-Skene label-noise models and validation (double) sampling; first checks: does the EM converge to the MLE and not depend on its start, are estimators compared at matched smoothing and on paired audit sets, does the headline survive noise, and is the classical double-sampling literature (Tenenbein 1970) and gold-question crowdsourcing work cited.

evidence.correctness: Reproduces: in a private copy `PYTHONPATH=src /usr/bin/python3.13 experiments/run.py` regenerated results.txt byte-identically in 47 s, and figure.py regenerated goldaudit.svg byte-identically. Independent re-implementation with no subject import (`/usr/bin/python3.13 -I /tmp/claude-0/goldaudit/scripts/indep.py mc`: own utility model written from the stated formulas, own exact scoring, own draws with a different RNG, own log-space Dawid-Skene-with-gold EM) gives blind 0.3824, true Bayes 0.3917 / 0.4066 (exact match to results.txt:4,26) and Monte Carlo cells within about 1-2 SE of the file: label 0.7 G=10 N=200 gold 0.3853 / noisy 0.3871 / pooled 0.3873 / EM 0.3900 (file 0.3857 / 0.3874 / 0.3877 / 0.3903); label 0.9 G=10 N=200 0.3947 / 0.3987 / 0.3993 / 0.4053 (file 0.3949 / 0.3985 / 0.3990 / 0.4054); G=25 N=0 0.3878 / 0.4012 (file 0.3881 / 0.4009); label 0.9 G=200 N=1000 0.4063 / 0.3995 / 0.4008 / 0.4064 (file identical). EM convergence: on 800 audit sets the subject's EM at 2000 iterations equals 20,000 iterations and equals my own EM to 5.6e-16 (`cd /tmp/claude-0/goldaudit/scripts && /usr/bin/python3.13 emiters.py`). Every README number traces to results.txt (checked all 5 results). Not 4: the small-G EM-vs-gold gap is partly a smoothing artefact (see domain).
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: 7 tests (7 passed, 0.25 s); run.py writes results.txt ('about a minute': 47 s) and gold.png; figure.py and goldaudit.svg present and in sync; sim.py 'is a copy' of ambient-noisyaudit (diff: identical); homepage entry research/_homepage/projects.json:1896 and research/README.md:446 present. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/ambient-goldaudit/ could not be loaded (proxy 403), so the served copy is unchecked. No stubs or TODOs; README Limitations and Next steps are honest and the next step (pricing) was done in ambient-auditbudget.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`: 7 passed in 0.25 s. Good population-limit tests (gold-only converges; joint EM recovers C, A and prior at n = 220k; EM with N = 0 equals gold-only). Five mutants via quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (dropping gold from the EM M-step; transposing the gold count matrix), 3 survived: replacing the Bayes label-to-mode rule with the blind mode (est.py:88), dropping the prior weight in value() (est.py:93), and starting EM at auditor accuracy 0.4 (est.py:62). The decision step that turns every estimate into a utility is untested: the only test of it (tests/test_est.py:43) asserts value >= blind - 1e-12, which the blind policy itself satisfies. No test pins any result number.
evidence.craft: Read est.py, sim.py, run.py, figure.py, tests/test_est.py, pyproject.toml. est.py is short, vectorised (einsum E-step), docstrings precise, pseudo-counts guard zero cells. Defects: figure.py carries a dead `table()` helper and an `if not logy: pass` no-op (figure.py:24, 72-73) copied from a template; two figures (gold.png from run.py, goldaudit.svg from figure.py) with the README embedding only gold.png; sim.py is a verbatim copy (disclosed, but the ambient-* lineage now holds many copies); run.py is a flat script; gold_only and joint_em default to different smoothing (alpha 1.0 vs 0.5) without a stated reason.
evidence.claims: Disclosure is honest (stylised, AI-assisted, EM started at the true accuracy, uniform errors, 150 sets, no pricing). Backed: results 1, 3, 4, 5 and the reference values (all traced to results.txt). Not backed: projects.json:1898 (served summary) 'Pooling noisy with gold audits as truth is worse than gold alone' and README.md:44 heading 'Pooling the noisy audits as truth hurts' are unconditional, but at G = 10 pooled beats gold alone in all four cells (label 0.7: 0.3877 vs 0.3857, 0.3880 vs 0.3855; label 0.9: 0.3990 vs 0.3949, 0.3993 vs 0.3950; results.txt:9-10,31-32), and at G = 25, N = 200, label 0.7 they tie (0.3879 vs 0.3880). README.md:45 'almost matches it at label 0.9 (0.4054 vs 0.4046, ahead)' contradicts itself: 0.4054 > 0.4046 so it beats it. 'Using the noisy audits properly helps a lot' at small G: part of the gap is the smoothing mismatch (domain), not stated.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could build on the code (clean, fast, reproducible), and ambient-auditbudget already did. But the question is a classical one: estimating a misclassified categorical distribution with a fallible classifier plus a validation subsample of true labels is Tenenbein's double-sampling scheme (Tenenbein 1970, JASA 65; 1972, Technometrics), and combining gold questions with noisy crowd labels in Dawid-Skene EM is standard in crowdsourcing (Raykar et al. 2010 JMLR 'Learning from crowds'; Oleson et al. 2011 'Programmatic gold'; Wang, Ipeirotis & Provost on gold vs redundant labels); prediction-powered inference (Angelopoulos et al. 2023, Science) is the modern gold-plus-noisy framing. None is cited; only Dawid & Skene and Horvitz. With a gold subset the latent-class model is identified, so 'EM with gold beats gold alone and the gap closes as G grows' is the expected result, and 'noisy read as truth is biased and does not improve with N' was already the parent project's finding. Novelty: the decision-utility framing on this stylised assistant model only.
evidence.domain: The EM is the standard semi-supervised latent-class MLE (gold rows enter the C and prior counts, noisy rows through the posterior) and I confirmed it converges and matches an independent implementation. Departures a reviewer flags: (a) unmatched smoothing: gold_only uses alpha = 1 and joint_em 0.5; at label 0.9, G = 10, gold_only at alpha 0.5 scores 0.3979 against 0.3948 at alpha 1 on the same 150 sets, about 30% of the reported EM-vs-gold gap (`/usr/bin/python3.13 /tmp/claude-0/goldaudit/scripts/confounds.py`); (b) EM started at the true auditor accuracy (disclosed); I checked starts 0.5 and 0.95 give the same result to 0.0009, but a start of 0.34 (near chance) drops label 0.7 G=10 N=1000 from 0.3905 to 0.3867; (c) estimators are compared across cells with different RNG seeds and as std, not SE or paired differences, though within a cell all four share audit sets; (d) only one auditor accuracy, one mix and uniform errors (disclosed).

defects.what: Served summary says 'Pooling noisy with gold audits as truth is worse than gold alone' and README result 2 is headed 'Pooling the noisy audits as truth hurts', unconditionally; at G = 10 pooled beats gold alone in all four cells (label 0.9, N = 200: 0.3990 vs 0.3949) and ties at G = 25, N = 200, label 0.7. It hurts only from about 25-50 gold audits up.

The Bayes label-to-mode rule and the value() scorer, which turn every estimate into the reported utility, are untested: replacing the rule with the blind mode, or dropping the prior weight in value(), leaves all 7 tests green (the only test asserts value >= blind, which blind satisfies). No test pins a result number.

gold_only (alpha 1.0) and joint_em (alpha 0.5) are compared at different smoothing; at label 0.9, G = 10 gold_only at alpha 0.5 scores 0.3979 vs 0.3948, about 30% of the EM-vs-gold gap that result 3 attributes to 'using the noisy audits properly'.

Nearest prior work not cited: Tenenbein (1970, JASA) double sampling with a fallible classifier and a true-label validation subsample is this exact design; semi-supervised Dawid-Skene with gold questions (Raykar et al. 2010; Oleson et al. 2011; Wang, Ipeirotis & Provost) and prediction-powered inference (Angelopoulos et al. 2023). With gold the model is identified, so the ordering found was expected; novelty is the stylised utility framing only.
Result 3 says joint_em at G = 10 'almost matches' gold_only at G = 50 at label 0.9 '(0.4054 vs 0.4046, ahead)': it is ahead, so it beats it; the sentence contradicts itself.

Estimators in different cells are compared with std only (no SE or paired difference), and each cell uses its own RNG seed, so cross-cell comparisons such as 'G = 25 matches the noisy reading' rest on unpaired means.
figure.py carries a dead table() helper and an `if not logy: pass` no-op from a template; two figures (gold.png, goldaudit.svg) are produced but the README embeds only gold.png.

verdict: A small, clean, bit-reproducible (47 s) stylised simulation whose numbers are right: an independent re-implementation (own utility model, own draws, own EM) reproduces the reference utilities exactly and every Monte Carlo cell I checked within 1-2 SE, and the EM converges to the same MLE as my own to 1e-16. The weaknesses are around the numbers: the served summary's 'pooling is worse than gold alone' is false at G = 10 in all four cells; about 30% of the headline EM-over-gold gain at small G is a smoothing mismatch (alpha 1 vs 0.5); the decision rule and scorer are untested (3 of 5 mutants survive, including replacing the Bayes rule with the blind one); and the design is Tenenbein's classical double sampling, uncited, so the ordering was expected. Correct but not at the reviewer bar on claims and verification; does not meet the bar.
